## Use of AI

AI tools are welcome for writing code, tests, and PR descriptions. You're responsible for understanding, testing, and reviewing anything AI-generated before you submit it. See [AI_DEVELOPMENT_GUIDE.md](AI_DEVELOPMENT_GUIDE.md) and [AI_GUARDRAILS.md](AI_GUARDRAILS.md) for the guardrails our own AI agents follow.

Conventions for writing code live in each area's `AGENTS.md`; rules for reviewing it live in [`REVIEW.md`](../REVIEW.md), which every AI reviewer loads. If a review bot keeps raising the same false positive, add a "do not flag" entry to `REVIEW.md`. If reviewers keep catching the same mistake, add a one-line rule to the matching `AGENTS.md`.

documents.AGENTS.md:
**Path Resolution Override & Precedence:** the User Layer lives under the data root, resolved in this order:
1. **Environment Variables:** `CAREER_OPS_ROOT` or `CAREER_OPS_DATA_DIR` (a relative path resolves against the repository root). An override, here or in the marker file, inside a Claude Code plugin install copy is refused: `getCareerOpsRoot()` throws `UnsafeDataRootError`.
2. **Marker File:** a `.career-ops-data` file in the repository root holding an absolute or relative path to the user data directory.
3. **Plugin Install Default:** `~/career-ops-data` when the code runs from a Claude Code plugin install copy (inside `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`, `marketplaces/` or `synced/`), which every plugin update replaces. See `docs/CLAUDE_PLUGIN.md`.

### Auto-memory scope (clarification, not exception)

Auto-memory at `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/` is for **behavioural steering only**: preferences (style, tone, cadence), process rules and corrections, operational state (active relationships, applied roles, observed patterns, outcome learnings), and external references. It holds no content claims about the user's work, accomplishments, or authorship. A fact that belongs in user-facing content lives in the user-layer files.



Output: `{"onboardingNeeded": <bool>, "data_root": "<path>", "project_root": "<path>", "missing": [...], "unpersonalized": [...], "warnings": [...], "autoCopied": [...]}`. `data_root` holds every user-layer file (`data/`, `cv.md`, `config/profile.yml`, `portals.yml`, etc.) and `project_root` is the code checkout. In a split checkout (the `.career-ops-data` marker or an exported `CAREER_OPS_ROOT` / `CAREER_OPS_DATA_DIR`), operate on `{data_root}`, except where a per-file override (`CAREER_OPS_TRACKER`, `CAREER_OPS_PROFILE`) names that file. `missing` lists whichever of `cv.md`, `config/profile.yml`, `modes/_profile.md`, `portals.yml` are absent; `warnings` holds non-blocking setup signals. The command is read-only: `autoCopied` stays empty unless onboarding adds `--init-templates`.

**`dataRootError` is a hard stop.** Doctor exits non-zero and reports it (`{code, source, root}`, with `data_root` null and the refusal in `warnings[0]`) when the data root sits inside a Claude Code plugin install, where the next plugin update deletes every write. Do not onboard on this state: no `--init-templates`, no `cv.md`, no tracker. Show the user the refusal from `warnings[0]`, wait for them to point `dataRootError.source` at a folder outside `~/.claude/plugins` (or remove it to use the default data root), then run doctor again. `modes/_onboarding.md` → "When the data root is refused" says when that fix needs a session restart.

**Act on `unpersonalized` even when `onboardingNeeded` is false.** Entries are `{path, reason, impact}` for a personalization file that still carries template content, or a `config/profile.yml` or `portals.yml` that holds only comments. An unedited `_profile.md` scores every A-F evaluation against the **template author's** archetypes and North Star; an unedited `_brief.md` hands triage literal `{placeholders}`. An empty or comments-only YAML prerequisite also sets `onboardingNeeded` to true; an unpersonalized Markdown template stays a warning. Before running `scan`, `pipeline`, or `batch` with a non-empty `unpersonalized`, tell the user which files it lists, with each entry's `impact`, and offer to personalize them from their CV first. For `modes/_profile.md`, say that every score changes. Doctor never reports `modes/_custom.md`: unedited house rules are a valid end state.

**We accept issues, not pull requests.** Design and implementation are done by
the repository maintainers. If you've already built a fix or feature locally,
share **the prompt you used** to produce it, not the source code. This applies
to everyone outside the repository maintainers, including organization members
who happen to have write access to this repository.

## Who opens pull requests

Pull requests against this repository are opened by the **repository
maintainers** only. That includes organization members with write access: being
able to push a branch here is not the same as being asked to. The constraint is
the workflow described above, not permissions.

If you're not a repository maintainer, open a **detailed issue** instead and a
maintainer will pick it up. A pull request from anyone else is closed with a
pointer back to this document; if it held a fix worth keeping, a maintainer files
an issue for it first, so the work is not lost.

We support using AI (i.e., LLMs) as tools when contributing to Open Home Foundation projects. However, you are responsible for any contributions you submit, and we are responsible for any contributions we merge and release. We hold a high bar for all contributions to our projects.

Our maintainers dedicate their time and expertise to reviewing contributions. Submitting AI-generated content that you have not personally reviewed and understood wastes that time and will not be accepted.

## Autonomous agents

**We do not allow autonomous agents to be used for contributing to our projects.** We will close any pull requests or issues that we believe were created autonomously, and may mark automated comments as spam. This includes contributions that bypass the provided issue or pull request templates.

documents.llvm/docs/AIToolPolicy.md:
An important implication of this policy is that it bans agents that take action
in our digital spaces without human approval, such as the GitHub [`@claude`
agent](https://github.com/claude/). Similarly, automated review tools that
publish comments without human review are not allowed. However, an opt-in
review tool that **keeps a human in the loop** is acceptable under this policy.
As another example, using an LLM to generate documentation, which a contributor
manually reviews for correctness, edits, and then posts as a PR, is an approved
use of tools under this policy.

AI tools must not be used to fix GitHub issues labelled [`good first
issue`][good-first-issue]. These issues are generally not urgent, and are
intended to be learning opportunities for new contributors to get familiar with
the codebase. Whether you are a newcomer or not, fully automating the process
of fixing this issue squanders the learning opportunity and doesn't add much
value to the project. **Using AI tools to fix issues labelled as "good first
issues" is forbidden**.
